claim: On a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q workstation with PCIe 4 host links and no NVLink or InfiniBand, training a 500M-param MoE at ~100k tokens per microbatch showed gradient communication at 50% of single-step time and matmul at only ~20%.
stance_target: The premise that DDP communication dominates per-microbatch step time on a no-NVLink PCIe box
scope_conditions: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, PCIe 4, no NVLink/IB; Qwen3-style MoE 500M total / ~330M active; ~100k tokens/microbatch; second-hand write-up of a talk
quoted_support: on a PCIe 4 bus without high-speed interconnects, gradient communication accounted for 50% of the single-step time, while matrix multiplication took up only about 20%

claim: Pairing the ~100k-token microbatch with gradient_accumulation=10 (effective global batch ~1M tokens) and DDP.no_sync() so the all-reduce fires only on the 10th accumulation step cut wall-clock from under 18 hours to 13.2 hours.
stance_target: The pipeline's position that DDP overhead at 1M-token global batches is small once gradient accumulation is used
scope_conditions: Same box; effective batch ~1M tokens; 10B-token dataset
quoted_support: Zach used a microbatch size of roughly 100k tokens paired with gradient_accumulation=10, forming an effective batch size of approximately 1M tokens ... overall training time naturally plummeted from 18 hours down to 13.2 hours

claim: 4-GPU DDP on this PCIe-4 no-NVLink box delivered only ~2.6x over single-GPU rather than the ideal 4x.
stance_target: The assumption that DDP scales near-linearly on a thin wire
scope_conditions: 4x RTX PRO 6000, PCIe 4, no NVLink; 500M MoE
quoted_support: Simply expanding the unoptimized baseline configuration to four-GPU DDP yielded a measured ~2.6x speedup

claim: The case study is a 500M-parameter model on PCIe 4 (~25 GB/s), so its absolute numbers do not transfer to a 1B+ model on PCIe Gen2 x4 (~1 GB/s); only the mechanism (accumulation amortises sync) transfers.
stance_target: The transferability of this measurement to the CMP 170HX box
scope_conditions: Author's own boundary statement: micro-level conclusions do not transfer across scale
quoted_support: techniques effective on a single GPU may no longer hold at a different scale ... micro-level findings from small experiments cannot be treated as universal rules of thumb
